change_class_rationale: Reviewer-requested repair to Cloud PRD markdown and JSON evidence. No source code, schema, runtime contract, or workflow changes.
task: Resolve PR #128 review findings for Cloud hyperscaler audit honesty, portfolio scope, stale Foundry gaps, source traceability, and benchmark-heading compatibility.
local_gates: cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate product-index: PASS (7 axis rows, 20 catalog products)
cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate quality-lanes: PASS (69 registry records, 69 markdown rows, 64 active commands, 39 owner teams)
verification_limitations: cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate benchmark --products-dir docs/products was run and improved from 12 to 11 failures after Cloud gained the exact `## Competitive benchmark` heading. Remaining failures are pre-existing non-Cloud PRDs: docs/prds/{ontology,application,payroll,tenancy,foundry,workflow,accounting,connect,INDEX,hr}.md and docs/products/foundry/PRD.md.
Full GitHub CI must be re-run after push because this repair rebases PR #128 onto the #126 merge head.

findings: The repair scopes the audit instead of pretending it scored every product family. Excluded Connect and Enterprise specs are listed explicitly.
Cloud prose-only Strong scores were downgraded to Adequate in both the JSON scorecard and the PRD adoption summary where no CI/test or concrete enforcement mechanism is cited.

Foundry gaps were reconciled against current dev after PR #126: queue-depth shedding and p99 capability SLOs are no longer listed as missing; the remaining all-providers-degraded terminal shed state is still tracked.
No retired registries/cross-cutting path is introduced. The repair adds only doc/evidence artifacts.
Audit-chain row and multispectrum repair evidence make the review/fix loop traceable.

architect.rationale: The audit remains useful while no longer claiming portfolio-wide or enforcement-backed maturity that the evidence does not prove.

guardrails: Do not promote this core-subset scorecard to portfolio-wide status until Connect and Enterprise product specs are scored.
Do not use Strong for prose-only commitments unless the artifact names a CI lane, test, or concrete kernel/domain enforcement path.
